# Software and reproducibility

Record the exact repository commit, assay profile, haplotype catalogue, calibration
control manifest, model configuration, external database snapshots and commands
used for every result.

## Core commands

```bash
python scripts/compile_assay.py --help
python scripts/admit_amplicon_reads.py --help
python scripts/build_hba_family_map.py --help
python scripts/calibrate_amplicon_model.py --help
python scripts/genotype_amplicons.py --help
python scripts/benchmark_genotype_backend.py --help
python scripts/audit_truth_regions.py --help
```

## Required provenance per model result

Retain:

- Git commit and Python package version;
- assay ID/version and profile checksum;
- haplotype catalogue checksum and candidate count;
- family-map anchor and sequence checksums;
- molecule-admission configuration;
- calibration ID/status and control-manifest checksum;
- calibrated model-config checksum;
- execution backend and backend-build environment;
- sample/run/lot/operator stratum where governed and available;
- top class, alternatives, ambiguity/no-call reason; and
- exact output-file checksums.

## Truth-scoped benchmark provenance

For each WGS benchmark, retain the VCF and BED release identifiers, genome build,
contig naming, normalization/comparison command and exact target coverage from
`audit_truth_regions.py`. For amplicon evaluation, retain the orthogonal method by
event class and separate calibration controls from held-out blinded samples.

## Performance provenance

The backend benchmark must first pass numerical parity with the Python reference.
Record the frozen compiled assay and molecule-table checksums, candidate haplotype
count, observable class count, raw and grouped evidence counts, hardware, compiler,
NumPy/Cython/Python versions, warm-ups and all repeated timings. Do not report only
the minimum runtime.

The Quarto source is the manuscript authority. HTML is used for iterative review;
Typst produces the PDF and preserves the generated `.typ` source for final layout
inspection.
